The enrichment analysis identifies **Eicosanoid synthesis (Wikipathways WP167)** as the top pathway (FDR = 0.0, fold enrichment = 1000.76), driven by five of the input metabolites: arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717), and 5-HETE (C04805). A KEGG reaction-path query confirms that arachidonic acid is directly upstream of leukotriene A4 (bidirectional path of length 2 via intermediate C05356), consistent with the well-established 5-lipoxygenase–mediated branch of eicosanoid biosynthesis. A secondary high-confidence hit is the **Selenium micronutrient network (WP15)**, which clusters hypochlorite (C19697), copper (C00070), arachidonic acid, and multiple eicosanoids, reflecting the known intersection of oxidative-inflammatory signaling and trace-element homeostasis. Hypochlorite independently maps to Reactome "ROS and RNS production in phagocytes," linking the observed differential abundance to innate immune activation.

**Biological significance.** The co-enrichment of arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 suggests pronounced phospholipase-A2–driven liberation of arachidonic acid followed by divergent lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase fluxes. Leukotriene A4 is a highly reactive precursor to the cysteinyl leukotrienes that mediate bronchoconstriction and neutrophil chemotaxis; elevated 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 point toward 15-lipoxygenase activity and PPARγ activation, respectively—pathways associated with resolution of inflammation and metabolic regulation. The simultaneous presence of hypochlorite (a myeloperoxidase-derived oxidant produced by activated neutrophils) and copper (a cofactor for oxidative enzymes) reinforces an inflammatory mileu. Gentisic acid, dihydrothymine, and histamine, while not core eicosanoid pathway members, may reflect secondary antioxidant responses (gentisic acid) and mast-cell activation (histamine) that commonly accompany eicosanoid-driven inflammation.
